newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T edges higher, results at top of range.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T edges higher, results at top of range.

text.p: Shares in British tobacco and insurance conglomerate B.A.T Industries edged 4p higher in early trade encouraged by a nine percent rise in nine month pretax profits at the top end of the market range, said analysts.
B.A.T posted pretax profits of 2.039 billion stg in the nine months to September 30 against a market range of 2.0 to 2.050 billion.
"The numbers are almost exactly in line with expectations, in fact if anything towards the top end of the range," said BZW analyst Nyren Scott-Malden.
Tobacco trading profit of 1.265 billion, a seven percent increase over last year's record results, was also impressive, said analysts.
"It's also encouraging to see them talk tough with the U.S. trial lawyers," said one analyst who declined to be named.

Chairman Lord Cairns hit back at U.S. lawyers who have consistently claimed in litigation proceedings against the company's U.S. tobacco subsidiary Brian & Williamson that B.A.T knew all along that smoking causes diseases but kept it from the public.

The pace of U.S. litigation has caused some of its big UK shareholders to call for a demerger of B.A.T's U.S. tobacco business, enabling the company to put its effort into selling cigarettes in Asia and other emerging markets.

"One of the things that we do seem to be constantly accused of is that we had some great knowledge before anybody else that smoking causes diseases, not only have we never had that evidence we have never concealed anything from the public," said a company spokesman.
The company's shares have been sorely hurt by the stream of upsets and shifts in the progress of U.S. litigation.
B.A.T shares have fallen from a high of 585p on February 2 to 434p on Friday, shedding nearly four billion stg from the company's stockmarket value along the way.
On Tuesday Brown & Williamson urged a Florida judge to set aside a jury award of $750,000 to a smoker with lung cancer.

In the case of Grady Carter a jury in Jacksonville ruled in August that Brown & Williamson was negligent and made a dangerous and defective product. But B.A.T expects the Carter verdict to be overturned.
B.A.T executives are also expected to talk tough on U.S. tobacco litigation proceedings at an analysts meeting today.
Executives are also likely to bring up a study in Science Magazine published last week in which researchers claimed to have found the missing link in causation of lung cancer.

As well as the strong growth in tobacco sales analysts highlighted the postive performance of Farmers, the U.S. insurance unit, which reported profits up 9.0 percent to 467 million stg in the nine month period.
Management fees from the exchanges rose six percent, with increased average premiums across most personal lines of business and a higher number of policies in force.
However, Eagle Star's profits for the nine months were 32 million stg lower at 162 million.
